rows.currentScript: The left word reads stam_. You need a letter to close both words. Put p there for stamp and pond. The rest reach only one word, or miss both.
rows.whyRewrite: Misleading: "You need a letter to close both words." The letter ends the first word but STARTS the second; "close both" states the rule wrongly, and it is the very slip the wrong options catch. Working otherwise correct: stamp and pond; b gives bond only, a gives neither.

rows.currentScript: Look at crow_ on the left. The right letter ends it and opens the next. A n builds crown and nest. The others finish just one side, or neither.
rows.whyRewrite: Form: "A n builds crown and nest." is wrong English; the letter n takes "an" ("An n ..."). Working otherwise correct: crown and nest; d gives crowd only, b gives best only.

rows.currentScript: Start with spoo_. One letter must end it and begin the next. A n gives spoon and noise. Each other letter completes one word alone, or none.
rows.whyRewrite: Form: "A n gives spoon and noise." is wrong English; the letter n takes "an" ("An n ..."). Working otherwise correct: spoon and noise; f gives spoof only, p gives poise only.
